blocks.text: Iconic Images Gallery presents Reverence: The Photography of Paul Nicklen , an exhibition by the Canadian photographer, filmmaker and marine biologist. The show opens to the public at the gallery’s Piccadilly space on 12 November 2026 and runs until 2 January 2027. All photography will be available for purchase.

One of the most celebrated wildlife photographers working today, Nicklen has spent more than three decades photographing the polar regions, the open ocean and the animals that depend on them. Reverence: The Photography of Paul Nicklen marks his debut UK gallery exhibition.

The exhibition brings together several works spanning Nicklen’s career, from the ice shelves of Svalbard to the deep waters off Dominica. In Face to Face (Svalbard, 2014), a polar bear peers through the window of a remote cabin. Ice Waterfall (Svalbard, 2014) captures the awesome spectacle of meltwater pouring from a vast ice cap into the sea. Suspended Grace (Dominica, 2019) shows sperm whales sleeping upright beneath the surface, a rarely witnessed behaviour. Legend (Kenya, 2025) thrusts the viewer into the path of a 52-year-old elephant much respected by the Maasai who protect him. Each is produced as a limited edition print, signed and numbered by the photographer.

The title reflects the spirit of Nicklen’s work: awe, deep respect and a sense of connection with the natural world. His pictures are made under extreme conditions and often at close quarters, and they carry both the beauty of these places and the urgency of protecting them.

Carrie Kania, Creative Director of Iconic Images, says: “We are honoured to host Paul Nicklen’s first exhibition in the UK. Few photographers have gone so far, or so close, to capture a planet that is disappearing before our eyes, and fewer still bring such a sense of urgency to that awe. These photographs are a record of our world as it is now, and they’ll matter more with each generation that follows.”

Paul Nicklen says: “I am incredibly excited to bring Reverence to London for my first solo exhibition in the UK, and I am grateful to Iconic Images Gallery for making it possible. For decades, I have travelled to the most remote corners of our planet, trying to capture the beauty, fragility, and resilience of the natural world. Photography has always been my way of connecting people to places and species they may never have the opportunity to experience themselves. London has such a rich history of art, exploration, and conservation, and it feels like a wonderful place to share this body of work. My greatest hope is that people leave the exhibition feeling inspired, connected to nature, and reminded that we still have so much worth protecting.”

The exhibition coincides with the release of his latest book, also titled Reverence (Hemeria, 2026), the most comprehensive collection of Nicklen’s photography published to date. Three years in the making, the 360-page book gathers 160 photographs, including previously unseen work.
Reverence: The Photography of Paul Nicklen 12 November 2026 – 2 January 2027 Iconic Images Gallery Piccadilly 16 Waterloo Place, St James’s, London SW1Y 4AR www.iconicimagesgallery.com
